title: Self-serve verification and lightweight audit trail for published performance profiles
creator: Diego Ramirez
description: Background: Publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles is currently a gated, manual process that requires signoff from the perf team and the profile steward. This creates bottlenecks for rapid model onboarding and small iterative updates (quantization tweaks, micro-benchmarks, cost-recalculations). Goal: Build a self-serve verification flow that lets model stewards (product/ops/partners) publish minor performance profile updates with an attached lightweight audit trail and automatic sanity checks. The flow should retain strong guardrails for user-facing pins and high-impact changes while removing friction for low-risk profile refreshes. Scope: 1) Self-serve web UI and API for submitting profile updates with required inputs (benchmarks, sample traces, cost model). 2) Automated sanity checks (latency regression thresholds, throughput drop, cost delta limits, signature completeness). 3) Generate an immutable, human-readable audit record (timestamp, submitter, metrics, snapshot links) stored alongside the catalog entry. 4) Auto-approval path for low-risk updates and manual review for high-risk ones. Non-goals: Replacing the formal attestation/signing workflow for major model pins; cross-region normalization logic beyond basic checks.
acceptance_criteria: Product stewards can submit a profile update via Console or API with required artifacts (benchmark bundle link, sample traces, cost table)
Automated sanity checks run and produce pass/fail with detailed failure reasons surfaced in the UI
Low-risk updates (configurable thresholds) are auto-approved and published within 30 minutes of submission
Failed or high-risk submissions flag a manual review task for the perf team and block publish until signed off
An immutable audit record is written for every submission that includes submitter, timestamp, metric deltas, and artifact links
Audit records are queryable in Console and exported to S3/archival store with retention policy metadata
All published updates include a lightweight human-readable changelog and machine-friendly metadata (profile version, parent pin if applicable)
updates: 2025-02-20: Discovery interviews with eight model stewards and infra owners; primary friction is turnaround time for minor cost re-evaluations
2025-02-24: Prototype UI wireframes validated with two stewards; they want immediate feedback for failed checks and ability to attach mitigation notes
2025-02-27: Backend contract drafted with ENG for auto-checks endpoint and audit-record write API. Initial risk thresholds proposed: latency +10%, throughput -15%, cost delta +25%
2025-03-02: Engineering spike completed demonstrating proof-of-concept audit record stored as signed JSON blob in archival bucket; next: schema stabilization and RBAC checks
comments: Kenji (perf lead): 'Agree with auto-approval for cosmetic metadata changes; want conservative defaults for numeric thresholds.'
Mina (security): 'Audit record format must include hash of submitted artifact and identity proof; plan to reuse existing KMS signing flow.'
Sam (customer success): 'Need a view in Console that surfaces recently published low-risk changes to downstream teams; customers occasionally rely on cost numbers for billing estimates.'
decisions: Use a two-tier approval model: auto-approve for 'minor' updates (within thresholds) and manual review for all others
Audit records will be immutable and stored as newline-delimited signed JSON in the archival bucket (human-readable summary mirrored to Console)
Threshold defaults will be conservative but configurable per project/owner via a profile 'sensitivity' flag
tradeoffs: Quick publishing reduces time-to-value for stewards but increases risk of unnoticed regressions — mitigated by sampling post-publish smoke-tests
Storing verbose audit blobs increases storage cost; we will compress snapshots and prune raw artifacts after retention window
Tighter default thresholds will reduce auto-approvals and increase manual workload; looser thresholds increase blast radius
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha): Enable for internal model stewards only with a 'preview' flag; require perf-team manual review for any change that touches pin status
Phase 2 (Beta): Open auto-approval for low-risk updates; enable Console UI and API access for partner teams; telemetry collection for false-negatives/positives
Phase 3 (GA): Full rollout with configurable sensitivity profiles, SSO/RBAC controls, and archival retention SLA
tests: E2E: Submit a profile update that triggers a latency fail and verify UI surfaces failure reasons and blocks publish
E2E: Submit a low-risk cost-only update and verify it auto-publishes within SLA and writes an audit record
Integration: Verify audit record integrity by checking stored signature against KMS public key
Load: Simulate 100 concurrent submissions to validate queueing/throughput for auto-checks
